casting-call: Pipeline Flow and Routable Paths

The whole system after the simplification pass: one recording in, every path it can take out. Solid arrows are the main path. Amber dashed arrows are the fallback for when the far-side audio drops. Round-cornered gold boxes are the artifacts you keep. Three big things changed from the earlier version: the affect layer is gone, the MP4 remux is no longer a required step, and markers now ride inside the recording instead of a sidecar file.

The paths in words

Happy path. OBS writes an MKV that holds the two voice tracks and, when you use the buttons, a third marker track. The pipeline reads that MKV directly, so there is no remux to sit through. It pulls the two voice tracks out by stream index, checks each for silence before spending any time on Whisper, transcribes them, and weaves them into one [You] / [Caller] transcript. Then it cleans out the hallucinations Whisper invents on silence and folds in your markers.

Markers. This is the part that used to be a headache and no longer is. Each Stream Deck button plays a short "mark flag" / "mark action" clip onto Track 3, routed so the far side never hears it. Because that track is recorded on the same clock as the voice, a phrase at 14:32 lines up with 14:32 in the transcript with no alignment math at all. Whisper reads the track like any other, and each recognized phrase becomes an inline [MARKER] line dropped in at its moment. No sidecar file, no anchor, no plugin.

Dead-channel fallback. The silence check flags a sustained drop on the far-side track (Chrome App Audio Capture does this). When that happens the words only exist in the on-screen captions, so ripcap OCRs them and rebuilds the far side. The catch your first real recording exposed: the region is fixed, so the Meet window has to stay put. Move or resize it mid-call and one region no longer covers the whole thing.

What changed, and why

The remux stopped being mandatory. Transcription reads the MKV fine, so the MP4 is now an optional render (ripv) you make only when you want to watch a call back, with you on the left channel and the caller on the right. The MKV is the file you keep.

The affect layer is gone. The prosody and face-tracking scan caused more trouble than it earned, so it and its two heavy dependencies came out. That also un-broke the test suite.

Markers moved inside the recording. The old design logged button presses to a sidecar file stamped with wall-clock time, then tried to align them to the recording using a record_start anchor. OBS never wrote a reliable timestamp, which made that fragile. A sound on a third track has no such problem: it is already in the right place.
